## 2026.11.5


### OpenClaw v2026.11.5

For formatted release notes, [read this release on the docs site](https://docs.openclaw.ai/releases/2026.11.5).

OpenClaw v2026.11.5 lets you edit heartbeat checks in Automations, browse files alongside a chat, and run your agent’s chats through Requesty.

#### Heartbeat checks become editable jobs

Heartbeat checks, your agent’s periodic check-ins, are now editable Automations jobs for supported configurations. Instead of changing agent settings, you can edit each job’s schedule, prompt and delivery directly, and migrated checks keep their run history. See the [heartbeat migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat).

Supported managed updates run Doctor to convert existing checks. If you replace the binary manually, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Older Gateways cannot open the converted data, so returning to an older version requires a pre-upgrade backup with the matching build in a separate data directory. Plugin authors using the [removed heartbeat APIs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces#heartbeat-executor-and-wake-helpers) need to update their plugins before upgrading OpenClaw. Migrated jobs can deliver repeated updates and run without a configured route, so review delivery settings if you relied on the old behavior.



##### Heartbeat and Automations details


Job scratch is included in model context for session-target and standalone scheduled agent runs, so do not put secrets in it.

Command, task, hook and restart follow-ups that relied on heartbeat now run in ordinary sessions. Device notification changes and background command completions can reach their intended conversation without waiting for a heartbeat. A command result returned directly does not also produce a completion notice. Older Codex threads that still call `heartbeat_respond` may receive an unavailable-tool response.

Main-session agent-turn jobs retain Announce or owner delivery when edited in the Control UI or CLI. See [delivery guidance](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/delivery).

If Doctor keeps a conflicting or recreated `HEARTBEAT.md`, review it and copy any instructions you still want into the automation. If Doctor skips an older migrated task that still tries to send a quiet reply, update its prompt to use `NO_REPLY`. See the [Heartbeat migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/doctor/config-migrations).

See the [job scratch guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md#L320-L330).

Sources [#179387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179387) and [#180106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180106). Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

#### Chat panels and Files

The [chat panels](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/panels) bring files and tools alongside your conversation. Browse project folders and session files, search and preview a file beside the list, or use Review to read changes in a searchable file list. On desktop, you can move and resize the panel. On mobile, open [Details](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat#session-details) from the conversation title and move between Details and Panels without clearing your draft.

Files and Review also work on mobile. Files keeps your place as you browse and tells you when search results or attachment coverage are incomplete.

- [Panel layout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176356), [mobile Details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176527) and [panel navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176653) let you move between session information and available tools.

#### Requesty

OpenClaw now works with [Requesty](https://www.requesty.ai/) for AI inference. Requesty’s service offers 600+ models from 30+ providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, and teams can [set Requesty to mask personal information](https://www.requesty.ai/security), such as names and email addresses, in prompts before they reach a model provider.



##### Requesty sources


- [Requesty setup and model selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180788) · [commit ed083ae](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ed083ae19c89ded11a827814ece98812aca6c770). Thanks to [@lavicosa](https://github.com/lavicosa) and [@hannesrudolph](https://github.com/hannesrudolph) for contributing, and [@Thibaultjaigu](https://github.com/Thibaultjaigu) for filing the earlier [feature request #54444](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54444).

Model discovery lists managed chat models available to your key and does not account for region-specific policies. If discovery fails, three built-in choices remain available. See [Using Requesty with OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/requesty).



#### Conversation-linked automations

Scheduled automations with an exact link to the conversation that created them can use its memory and update its dashboard, including eligible widget pins. Jobs from an owner's direct chat can use owner-private memory while the requester remains an owner; jobs from group or non-owner chats use only that conversation's memory.

If the linked conversation is removed or archived, or its worktree is gone, the next scheduled run is skipped and the job pauses. Command jobs are exempt from this check. Restore the conversation or worktree and run `openclaw automations enable <jobId>` to resume it. A `/new` reset lets the job run without the old conversation's access. [Automation troubleshooting](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting)



##### Conversation-linked automation sources


- [Conversation availability and resume behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178965). Thanks to [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).
- [Dashboard reads, edits and eligible widget pins](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179011) and [conversation memory within its permission limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179062). Resetting or removing the conversation cuts off inherited access and new dashboard edits or pins; new edits and pins are also blocked after the run finishes. Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).



#### Persistent automations

Persistent automations can watch a command's output in a supported [local Docker sandbox](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#sandboxed-streams). When your execution policy asks for approval, an agent-created Gateway watcher request shows what will run, where it runs, where its output goes and that it can continue after the conversation and restart automatically.

Before downgrading, stop sandboxed streams, wait for them to settle and keep a verified backup. Older versions quarantine these jobs, and upgrading again does not restore them automatically.



##### Persistent automation sources


- [Watcher approvals](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177941) apply to the saved watcher; a refusal leaves an existing watcher unchanged, and reopening the conversation restores a pending request. Approval does not mean it started or stopped.
- [Docker sandbox streams](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177942) start in a fresh dedicated container without falling back to the host. Thanks [@joshavant](https://github.com/joshavant) and [@eleqtrizit](https://github.com/eleqtrizit) for both changes.



#### Scheduled plugin follow-ups

Plugins can schedule one-time or recurring follow-ups from eligible authenticated commands, so work can continue later in the same conversation. Each run checks the original requester's current permissions and saves its results to that conversation without posting to the channel. See [scheduled plugin commands](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work#requester-admitted-scheduled-commands).

Newly accepted schedules marked to survive a Gateway restart can continue if the matching plugin code and command remain available. Eligible requester-approved commands from core-bundled plugins also need the same identifiable packaged build; a different build or a disabled plugin ends their schedule at its next run. An occurrence that may already have started is skipped after restart.



##### Scheduled plugin follow-up details and sources


The original deadline and remaining runs are retained across a supported restart. The [background work guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime/background-work) explains eligibility and re-enrollment. Rolling back to a host without the applicable continuity support can retire a schedule at its next occurrence.

#### Models and Usage

Models brings your provider accounts and access together, while Usage shows your local session spending, activity and cost charts. Expand a provider in Models to see its accounts and available plan information, test its connection or manage access. When you remove a provider, OpenClaw asks before deleting saved accounts or eligible API keys, which may be shared.

Usage loads session totals and charts independently of provider plans. Its daily chart breaks down tokens and costs by provider, and the calendar stays visible when you select a day. If a provider does not report usage, totals can understate what you used or were charged. Usage with no known price is marked Unpriced.



##### Models and Usage sources


- Provider settings and external secrets stay in place when a provider is removed. Interrupted removals report what completed.

#### Utility model fallbacks

Utility tasks can use their own backup models, independently of the main chat model’s fallback list. Titles, progress narration, Activity recaps, composer predictions, Side chat and transcript summaries can try those models in order after a retryable failure. Backup providers can receive the task’s content, so choose providers you trust with that data. [Utility model settings](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-agents/models)

#### Personal sidebar Sections

Organize conversations in personal Sections below Pinned in the Control UI sidebar. Create a Section from **Filter & sort** or a session’s **Add to section** menu, then choose a source and find conversations by owner or search beyond the loaded sidebar. Drag conversations into a Section and reorder Section headers. Adding a conversation organizes your sidebar without giving anyone access. Child conversations stay with their parent, and removing a Section keeps its conversations.

Sections sync for profiles with general Gateway write access. On restricted or profileless connections, they stay in the current browser. See [Sessions and the sidebar](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui).

#### Agent and session navigation

**Show all agents** in the Control UI sidebar now shows one row per agent. Pin an agent above the roster, select its avatar to open its main chat, or use its menu to open **Sessions** or **Settings**. Rows show when an agent is busy and preview its latest available assistant reply.

The **Sessions** page brings search, refresh, filters and **New session** together, with an **Agent** column in the all-agent view and a message when transcript search is unavailable. Sessions and Worktrees share the same title and tab layout. In team mode, the chat header identifies the agent and opens that conversation’s session and workspace actions. [Sessions and sidebar](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar)

Agent pins are saved in your browser profile and shared with the agent switcher. Sidebar previews come from visible, non-archived sessions.

- [Agent roster and Sessions navigation, #174984](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174984) — Thanks [@Patrick-Erichsen](https://github.com/Patrick-Erichsen).



#### Session changes during reconnects

Keep organizing conversations while the Control UI reconnects. You can rename a session, change its icon, color or existing category, add or remove message reactions, and archive, unarchive or delete eligible sessions, including bulk archive and delete. Changes appear immediately and are sent after reconnecting to the same Gateway and account with unchanged credentials. Rejected changes are undone and show an error.

Keep the tab open until changes are sent. Closing or reloading it loses unsent changes. The English chat header also identifies a saved conversation while reconnecting or disconnected. See [queued session changes](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/offline-and-reconnect#queued-session-changes).

#### Stop across devices

You can use Stop in the [Control UI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat) on another device to stop work you started, even after the original device disconnects. This covers active runs, queued messages and follow-on work OpenClaw is still tracking. You need to be signed in as the same person with access to the conversation, and this doesn’t let you stop someone else’s work.



##### Stop across devices sources


- [PR #187408](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187408). Thanks to shakkernerd.



#### Independent sessions

You can ask an authorized agent to start separate work in a persistent session you can open and continue yourself. Give it a first message to start work immediately or have it create the session for later. If the first run fails, check whether the session was created before retrying.

#### Plugin reloads

Your agent can keep working through a plugin reload when the plugin opts in to [continuing active turns](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-runtime#reload-safe-plugins). Running tool calls finish before the turn moves to the reloaded plugin, including for compatible context engines. A plugin that has not opted in waits for the whole turn. Reload status shows which plugins can hand over and which are keeping a reload waiting.



##### Plugin reload sources


- [Turn handover](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185315) · [commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0957af25689d833a3afe685f0c723c77a1c68e78).
- [Context-engine handover](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185544) · [commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/522e44a5335945ab12275864dcca04ecc7623b49). Context engines must save turn state durably; a turn ends with an error if the replacement no longer provides its configured engine.
- Thanks [@jalehman](https://github.com/jalehman).



#### PostgreSQL storage

You can choose SQLite or PostgreSQL separately for shared state, agents, Workboard, Logbook and Team Reports. SQLite remains the default. Qualified PostgreSQL 16–18 configurations with UTF8 server and client encoding are supported for all five stores. Agent data includes transcripts, text search and shared authentication profiles. [PostgreSQL guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/postgresql)

Changing a setting does not move existing data. You can [port database families](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-engines#mixed-engines) between SQLite and PostgreSQL while the Gateway and embedded agents are stopped, and make matched backups of supported mixed-engine installations. Matrix account and encryption data, including retained data from disabled accounts, are included while the Matrix plugin is installed. Moving or restoring Team Reports requires its matching plugin and excludes temporary collected activity. Keep Logbook frame images and their referenced paths when moving or restoring them. If you already use global PostgreSQL with SQLite Team Reports, set the Reports storage choice to match its existing data before use.

[Backup recovery](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/backup) supports PostgreSQL stores, including retained Matrix data. PostgreSQL backups require the Gateway to be stopped, and restores run offline with the archived configuration and recovery server connection secret. If you rely on an older archive, make a fresh backup on the source installation for automatic recovery of plugin stores. Exact backups contain secrets. If a port reports pending or uncheckable legacy SQLite repairs, enable any named disabled plugin and run `openclaw doctor --fix` while the affected stores still use SQLite before retrying. A completed SQLite-to-PostgreSQL move keeps existing local client credentials usable. See [database engines](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-engines), [porting existing stores](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-engines#port-existing-stores) and [TLS and exec connection setup](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/postgresql#tls-and-exec-connection-qualification).

#### Decisions for plugins

Plugin developers can ask a supported Decision model to score or rank options, and the model can decline to answer instead of being forced to guess. Decision V2 also supports per-question errors and, where the provider offers them, sorting, tags and image questions. [OpenRouter Jev](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openrouter#typed-decisions-with-jev) can evaluate a PNG or JPEG, and Jev 1.14 and its latest alias can return a bounding box. Image and box support are experimental. See the [Decision SDK guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-overview/capabilities.md).

If a previously working Decision call is blocked, check that the plugin allows the chosen model. Images are sent to the selected provider.



##### Decisions sources

#### Daybreak Access

You can choose an available Daybreak Access level in chat or a new session without changing your model or Speed. OpenClaw keeps an available choice when you reopen a chat, start a new one or reset a session. Daybreak is also available with eligible OpenAI API keys, including in native Codex.

Admins need to [grant Blue and Red Access separately](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/operator-scopes#access-program-grants) for named Gateway roles. Model permission and provider eligibility also apply.

If you use a retired Daybreak Blue or Red model alias, check your configuration, saved chats and scheduled jobs, then [choose a replacement model and Access program](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openai/models#daybreak-alias-retirement).



##### Daybreak Access sources


- [Access choices and alias retirement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812). When no Access choice is saved, eligible requests can recover on the selected model and account instead of switching to a retiring alias. Unavailable saved choices are rejected rather than silently changed. Thanks [@VACInc](https://github.com/VACInc).
- [Separate grants and saved choices](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184930) · [commit ad9b7aec](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ad9b7aec3fa6ca1e070a89e0c48185199787355d). An explicit Standard choice is kept during retries, and removing a grant requires fresh authorization for queued and recovered work. Thanks [@VACInc](https://github.com/VACInc) and [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).
- [Saved chat choices](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185039) · [commit 3e1eff7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e1eff7f703c7cf69abf810e2e62c04e6380c678). Turning Daybreak off selects Standard; turning it on restores the last available Blue or Red choice for that agent. If access cannot be checked, the saved choice is kept without offering unconfirmed options. The displayed Access default matches the requested default on supported OpenAI routes, and reopening a chat no longer loads New Session setup to restore it. Thanks [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).
- [Eligible API-key access](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184451) fixes missing options and rejected requests. Native Codex supports eligible ChatGPT and Platform API-key accounts. The same change prevents a pending share action for a replaced chat from affecting the new session. Thanks [@VACInc](https://github.com/VACInc) for Daybreak and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) for the sharing fixture work.
- [Doctor and retired aliases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184519) · [commit 5685d2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5685d2f87b9fb840c674d6d6a5e88a48aa92c4cf). [Doctor](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/doctor/running) can find retired selections with `openclaw doctor --lint --only openai/daybreak-alias-retirement`. `openclaw doctor --fix` removes the obsolete failover target, but does not choose a replacement. References it cannot safely replace remain for review and retry. Thanks [@VACInc](https://github.com/VACInc).



#### Plugin-owned model credentials

Provider plugins can use credentials they manage for model requests. Requests remain tied to the owning plugin and are blocked if that authority is revoked or replaced. See the [provider plugin guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins.md).



##### Sources and complete change list


- Plugin-owned routes use their owner’s credentials exclusively. OpenAI Responses requests with these credentials use guarded HTTP. [#156799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156799). Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).



#### Agent avatars

With uploads enabled, the Control UI’s agent Identity editor lets you pick a Blobster preset or upload an image. If you have permission to generate avatars and the agent has a configured model, you can describe a new avatar and preview it before applying it. Avatar selections and changes to the agent’s name or emoji save automatically.

The agent’s avatar also appears in Control UI notices when a background session finishes and in supported browser push notifications, including approval alerts. Private notifications keep the generic icon.

#### Composer predictions

The Control UI can suggest a follow-up after a reply. Turn on **Composer predictions** in **Settings → Labs**, then press **Tab** or choose **Use suggestion** to put an editable draft in the message box. You decide when to send it.

Predictions are off by default and appear only in eligible empty composers. Read-only, imported and incognito conversations are excluded. Each active tab can make an extra model request per completed reply, which can add usage and cost. See the [Control UI chat guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat).

#### Android sidebar

The Android sidebar shows Gateway folders in their shared order, including empty folders, and lets you load more sessions. In wide, unobstructed flat windows, it stays beside the current page; compact windows use the drawer. Gateway folders are read-only in the Android sidebar.

#### Tauri desktop runtimes

The Tauri desktop app can include a runtime, so new local setups install the version bundled with the app. Existing local Gateways can switch to the bundled runtime from the tray. The macOS Tauri app now requires macOS 26.2 or later.

Experimental ahead-of-time runtimes can be bundled on glibc Linux x64 and arm64 and Apple silicon Macs. JIT remains the release default and the production choice on Linux, where quitting an AOT build can still require a forced stop. See [desktop build options](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/standalone#desktop-app-artifacts).



##### Desktop runtime sources


- To switch an existing local Gateway, start it and confirm **Use bundled runtime…** in the tray. On Windows, the switch supports JIT runtimes. After a successful switch, the app reloads the dashboard, updates its managed CLI and keeps the previous runtime for recovery.
- The manual Linux App workflow can package a prebuilt Linux x64 artifact. [#185885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185885). Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).



#### Telegram message widgets

[Telegram message widgets](https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/telegram/rich-messages) let your agent send interactive cards that update in place as you use them. Set `channels.telegram.widgets: true` to use them in compatible private bot chats, including private topics.

#### A2A task history

A2A peers can retrieve finished tasks after a Gateway restart for up to 24 hours. Retrying a message returns its retained task.



##### A2A task history sources


OpenClaw retains up to 500 finished tasks per account. A clean shutdown marks running tasks as failed. If storage rejects a result, the peer sees a failed task and can retrieve any completed artifact until expiry or the Gateway stops.

- [A2A task retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183490) · [709b1a1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/709b1a1ca3fe8179409004502b0491b853580d5e) · [A2A channel](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/channels/a2a.md). Thanks to [@ensignwesley](https://github.com/ensignwesley).



#### ClawRouter media

Use ClawRouter to generate speech for Talk and phone calls, create images from text with eligible GPT Image 2.5 Flare or Sunburst models, and transcribe audio files including Talk uploads with gpt-4o-transcribe. Image generation and transcription require access on your ClawRouter deployment and key; speech needs a key with speech access. Requests can count against your ClawRouter budget.

#### Browser page triage

Your agent can ask a Decision model whether a browser tab is still loading, has no results, or is showing a blocker such as a login screen or paywall. This advisory judgment works on supported text-capable Chromium and Lightpanda profiles, and an incomplete page reading can mislead it. The selected Decision provider receives a page excerpt, and hosted inference can incur charges. See [Decision models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/decision-models) and [supported browser profiles](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/browser/lightweight#page-classification-and-judge).

If an entered path is missing or isn’t a folder, the picker can open the device’s home folder. Writers enter the path manually, and the device validates the chosen folder when the session starts. #### Cold storage for large conversation histories

Cold storage can now archive inactive conversation history that used to stay in the active database because it was too large for one archive file. An entry that is too large to fit on its own stays in the active database. Existing archives still restore, and a missing or damaged piece of a new archive stops the restore before any history is brought back.

The upgraded database requires OpenClaw 11.5 or a compatible newer version. To roll back, restore a verified pre-upgrade backup with its matching OpenClaw version. [Agent database compatibility](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/reference/database-schemas/agent-schema-history.md)



##### Sources and complete change list


Supported backups include the new archives, and a full-history reset removes them.

- [#183827](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183827). Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete). [session maintenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance.md).



#### Managed sandbox base refresh

Before publishing to GitHub, you can ask your agent to update a [writable local managed sandbox](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/sandboxing/workspace-access#managed-project-workspaces) from the selected repository base while keeping your saved work and Git history. Resolve any reported conflicts and confirm the returned base commit, then run tests and Auto Review against the refreshed base. You can then update the same draft if you already have one. Refreshing does not publish anything. Finish any pending refresh and conflict resolution before downgrading.

#### Interactive plugin views

Compatible plugins can show interactive views beneath tool results in Control UI chat. Views return when you scroll back through history without rerunning the tool, and a saved text summary remains available when the view cannot be displayed.

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, including plugins enabled before this update. Native UI runs without a sandbox in each signed-in viewer’s browser with that viewer’s Gateway permissions. Existing opt-outs remain in effect. To turn it off for user-installed plugins, set `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins` to `false` and reload open Control UI tabs. The catalog warns before installation, and plugin details and enable reviews identify native UI.

#### Blind subagent evaluations

You can run blind evaluations with hidden native subagents in an isolated context. Set `blind: true` to omit model and session identities and the workspace path from prompts OpenClaw writes, including later turns and prompts for hidden native descendants. Tools and external harness instructions can still reveal those details. [Subagent tool reference](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md)

#### Gateway tool and automation policy

Gateway operators can set a [deployment-wide allowlist](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy#toolsgatewaypolicy) for model-directed tools and actions, including plugin tools and work started by an administrator. Tool Search, Code Mode and dedicated workers follow the same limit. It also limits the Gateway tools offered to [Codex](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness-reference/dynamic-tools) and enforces those limits when called. A restored conversation may still list an older tool, but the policy can deny its use.

GitHub publishing can be allowed as the explicit `publish` action, and an eligible child session can publish from its own workspace even when its parent cannot. Separate [automation controls](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy) can limit agents to jobs owned by their caller and restrict agent management of command jobs and watchers. Direct human administration, Codex-native tools and subagents, and local harness programs remain outside the tool allowlist. Restart or replace the Gateway after affected work finishes to apply policy changes.

#### Jev and TypeSafe decisions

Jev can answer Boolean, choice and score questions about text or structured data through OpenRouter or a compatible TypeSafe plugin. Hosted TypeSafe Jev also supports experimental questions about a single PNG or JPEG image. TypeSafe can connect to a System One server on another machine, so you can run inference separately from the Gateway. Evaluations send their evidence to the selected provider or server. See [TypeSafe setup](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/typesafe) and its [image formats and limits](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/typesafe#experimental-image-decisions).

#### OpenAI and ClawRouter Decisions

An explicit OpenAI Decision evaluation with GPT-6 Luna can include an inline PNG, JPEG or WebP image up to 4 MiB, and Decision V2 keeps the other answers when one question is refused. Evaluations send the supplied evidence to OpenAI and use Platform billing. Use a Platform API key with Decisions access. See [OpenAI Decision models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openai#decision-models).

Deployments that serve native Decisions can also select Luna through ClawRouter. Hosted availability was pending as of October 20, 2026, and access depends on the router key and service. See [ClawRouter Decisions setup](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/clawrouter#decision-models) and the [shared plugin SDK entry point](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md).

#### Skill Workshop drafts

In **Propose** mode, Skill Workshop saves what your agent learns as drafts so you can review changes before they reach your live skills. Open **Drafts** in the Control UI to apply or discard a draft, or use `/learn drafts` in chat. Applied updates to existing skills can be undone. See the [Skill Workshop guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skill-workshop#drafts).

Doctor brings earlier exported proposals into Drafts and keeps existing Propose settings. If your setting was previously switched to **Off**, choose **Propose** again to resume draft review.

#### OpenShell workers

Run an agent in a dedicated [OpenShell sandbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/gateway/openshell-workers.md) with brokered model access, and give it a private directory for documents shared across its sessions. A required worker profile applies to all Gateway sessions. Turns are blocked while the worker is unavailable, and bound documents are available while its node is connected.



##### Sources and complete change list


Setup requires OpenShell 0.1.3 or newer, a qualified Linux environment, matching Gateway and node builds, and a prepared provider policy and image. Worker mode initially supports one configured model through OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages. Exiting the foreground worker command stops the dedicated sandbox.

- [PR #168458](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168458) · [`38f411f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/38f411fbe793e749680aedbe53a9cfbd2afca5e3) · Thanks to [@sallyom](https://github.com/sallyom).



#### Sandbox Auto Review

Auto Review can inspect staged, unstaged and untracked Git changes in the sandbox where your agent is working. A restricted reviewer runs on the host, where provider credentials stay, and returns a validated report or a size error. See the [Auto Review guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/autoreview) for setup.

#### Gateway maintenance from chat

Owners can ask their agent to restart the Gateway it’s running on. The restart can wait for active work to finish, and OpenClaw sends a notice when the Gateway comes back. Restarts requested from external chat honor `commands.restart`. [Gateway restart guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/gateway/running)

You can also ask the agent to preview old update recovery copies eligible for cleanup. You can explicitly ask to delete those copies while the Gateway stays online. Deletion is permanent. Both actions are available in the minimal, coding, and messaging tool profiles, subject to owner permissions and tool restrictions. [Update recovery guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating)

#### Standalone Gateway and node services

Run managed Gateway and node services from a [standalone OpenClaw build](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/standalone) without a separate Node or Bun executable. Choose the standalone runtime and point it at the executable. Reinstalling or repairing the Gateway service retains that choice. Keep the whole build directory together, and rebuild older artifacts that lack the service runtime check.

#### Experimental standalone AOT builds

Experimental standalone AOT builds can run fetched CommonJS and TypeScript plugins, Node Code Mode cells and continuations, and QA Lab expressions and lambdas through an interpreter. You can also try compiling OpenClaw’s original TypeScript ahead of time. Both modes offer compiler controls for runtime trimming, locales and string-generated code. Interpreted paths can run more slowly, and JIT remains the default. An AOT-capable Bun build is required; leave strict string-code restrictions off if you rely on host NodeVM. See the [standalone build guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/standalone) and [runtime profiles](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/runtime-profiles).

#### Cloud worker Git history

Stop and reclaim can bring Git commits from a cloud worker back to a Gateway-managed worktree. OpenClaw adds the commits to the local branch when it can fast-forward safely. If histories diverge, the branch moves or staged changes conflict, OpenClaw brings back the files and leaves a note in the conversation explaining why it left out the commits.

Commit recovery needs a transfer that supports Git history. Large histories can still prevent reclaim over SSH. See the [cloud worker session lifecycle](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloud-workers/session-lifecycle).



##### Cloud worker Git history sources


- Reclaim preserves unpushed worker commits while keeping local edits and unrelated staged changes. Older native transfers return files only. [Report #110498](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/110498) · [#182140](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182140) · [Commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d6c29052f3294f9d49990728ae8d718829b49f89). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).



#### Cloud worker access for teams

Teams using cloud workers can let operators send sessions they created to specific cloud profiles without administrator access. Administrators grant profiles to a role, and operators with write access can choose a granted profile in New Session or eligible session placement controls. Profile setup, setup scripts and moves to the cloud still require an administrator. See [cloud worker dispatch](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloud-workers/dispatching-a-session).



##### Cloud worker access sources


- [Role-based cloud profile dispatch #186560](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186560). Thanks to galiniliev.



#### Remembered native runtime permissions

Administrators can remember permission for a native runtime on a specific agent, so supported new chats using that agent and runtime can start without asking again. Chats using remembered permission run with **Full access** and OpenClaw’s optional sandbox off. Mandatory sandbox and workspace policies still apply.

Remove the runtime from **Remembered native runtime permissions** in the agent’s settings to revoke remembered approval for later use. Approval given to an individual chat is managed separately. See the [agent configuration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-agents/entries-and-multi-agent).

#### Guest welcome conversations

Invited guests using [Visitor Access](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/reference/visitor-access) can land in a welcome conversation when they open Home, once per browser. It brings together their access expiry, available agents, any invitation note and guidance for getting started. A link to a specific conversation still opens that conversation.

Renewing an active invitation keeps the welcome conversation or unfinished setup and its note unless the note is replaced. Ending access leaves existing chats and transcripts in place, while a completed welcome conversation that is deleted stays deleted.

#### Gateway host-execution controls

Gateway operators can independently turn off terminals on the Gateway host and automations that execute there. Blocked jobs remain visible so you can disable or remove them. Authorized node terminals, sandbox-backed streams and scheduled agent turns remain available under their own policies.

Set `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_GATEWAY_LOCAL_TERMINALS=1` or `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_CRON_HOST_EXECUTION=1` in the Gateway launch environment and restart it. Both restrictions are off by default. The automation restriction covers saved jobs and manual runs. [Terminal settings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/web/control-ui/panels.md) · [Automation settings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md)

#### Agent Templates

Experimental Agent Templates let you browse official and community packages, inspect their publisher and contents, and add one to create an agent. Enable **Templates** in **Settings → Labs** to browse by category or explore Featured when it is available. Applicable trust reviews may ask for your acknowledgement before adding a package. When a Template includes a schedule, OpenClaw waits for the new agent to become available before installing it.

Administrators can choose **Create Template** from an agent’s sidebar, including for pinned agents, to prepare a private draft in its chat and review the contents before publishing to ClawHub. Review the package for personal information before submitting it. Publishing requires a workspace and ClawHub sign-in on the Gateway host, and a submission may be pending security review. See the [Templates guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/templates) and [creation guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/templates#create-with-an-agent).

If you used Claws, update old commands, links, configuration and Gateway API calls to use Templates. Existing Claws records carry over, but the former status, update, remove, export and migrate commands are no longer available. See the [current CLI commands](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/cli/templates.md).



##### Template sources


- [Community discovery and Add](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173345), [reviewed publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173346), and [creation in the agent’s chat](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173377). Thanks [@Patrick-Erichsen](https://github.com/Patrick-Erichsen).
- [Contents preview and chat handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171600) and [creating an agent with Add](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171623). If chat does not open after Add, retry without creating another agent. Adding the same Template again creates another agent without overwriting an existing workspace; shared plugins and MCP servers remain independently managed.
- [Featured and category browsing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178047) · [commit a4a0223b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a4a0223bc9bccc683698944c5c21145c810d4ea2). Category browsing ranks public Templates by installs; category search sorts the matches returned.
- [Scheduled Template Add](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178072) · [commit c909114f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c909114f55fc5889076bf4fbbb61f6ab32bf8146). A partial result is reported if the agent’s availability cannot be confirmed.

The review lets you inspect included items and edit the display name separately from the package name. Publishing shows progress and links to the Template.



#### Knowledge (experimental)

With experimental [Knowledge](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge), agents can save and find decisions, preferences and project facts along with their sources. Select Knowledge as your memory provider to turn it on. It replaces your previously active provider without deleting its data. You can browse records and their history in the Control UI, and agents can attach files already in their authorized workspace.

An administrator can give a specific group chat or channel read access to an agent’s private Knowledge, or allow it to read and save. Threads inherit access unless a more specific grant applies. Revoking access cannot take back information already retrieved by a conversation. [Stores and access](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge/stores-and-access)

If you are [moving from a separately installed copy](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge#moving-from-a-linked-or-path-install), save its settings, including store assignments, before uninstalling it. Restore them and the memory slot after enabling the bundled plugin.

#### Knowledge Scribes

[Knowledge Scribes](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge/scribes) can learn from conversations once or on a schedule, including archived conversations if you choose, or import selected Memory notes once without changing the originals. In the Control UI you can review and edit the prompt, check run history and manage scribes. Starting or controlling them requires Gateway write access, and they use your private access and the agent’s default model.

With Granola connected, a scribe can create Knowledge pages for meetings with transcripts and save their notes and transcripts. You choose the starting date, whether to include your own meetings or all meetings you can read, and a one-time or weekday schedule. Choosing all readable meetings includes their notes and transcripts in Knowledge. [Granola setup](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge/scribes#the-granola-plugin)

You can also enable Knowledge Consolidation to review unlinked claims weekly or nightly. Nightly runs can use more tokens, and private claim review requires an owner-authorized session. Regular nightly maintenance relinks claims without starting an agent review. [Maintenance guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/knowledge/maintenance)

#### PostgreSQL memory search

If your agent uses PostgreSQL, experimental [memory search](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/memory#postgresql-memory-search) can find indexed material by keyword, by meaning, or both. Semantic search needs the vector extension, while keyword-only search works without it. Memory and chat history searches also find words within dates, paths and filenames, with original punctuation in previews.

The search migration rebuilds text indexes once for existing PostgreSQL agent stores. Rolling it back requires the verified pre-upgrade backup and its matching build. [Storage changes](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes) · [PostgreSQL guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/postgresql)

Thanks [@lonexreb](https://github.com/lonexreb) and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete), and [@etzelm](https://github.com/etzelm) for reporting.

#### LanceDB table compaction

Use [`openclaw ltm optimize`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/memory-lancedb#compact-a-local-table) to compact a whole local LanceDB memory table across agents while keeping its rows and version history. Stop every Gateway and other process using the table, including external scripts, before running it, then restart the Gateways. The command reports fragment and row counts before and after. Keeping old versions means compaction may leave disk use unchanged.

#### GitHub pull requests in chat

Continue work on your own open or draft GitHub pull request in a Team conversation or an ordinary sandboxed chat. OpenClaw prepares an editable workspace. In a Team conversation, you can see the original PR and its checks, and eligible guests can publish back to it when shared publishing is configured. Prepare the PR again to bring in new commits while keeping your local work. [GitHub identity and shared publishing](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/github-identity)

In an ordinary sandboxed chat, earlier file links continue to open the original files read-only. Reopen a file from the new workspace before saving it.

#### GitHub pull request actions

Ask your agent to edit the title or description of a pull request shared from your session without publishing code. If you opened a managed PR, you can request another ClawSweeper review and upload screenshots or recordings from an eligible sandbox workspace. Review files before uploading them to GitHub. Eligible guests can edit their own session PR and mark their own existing draft ready for review without merging it. With full operator write access, you can inspect, close or merge a session-published PR. GitHub permissions, reviews and checks govern merges. [GitHub publishing guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/github-identity)

After a later publication fails, authorized users can edit, inspect or mark ready the last successfully published PR. Inspect the PR again if its head or publication changes.

#### GitHub publication from local chats

In a local chat that hasn’t been tied to a workspace, you can ask your agent to publish committed work from a local checkout to GitHub. Commit any pending changes first. OpenClaw works from a separate worktree, leaves your original checkout intact and brings the result back to the same conversation. [GitHub publication guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model)

#### Git co-author credit

Verified GitHub Enterprise participants can receive co-author credit on eligible shared-session commits published to the configured host. Credit is on by default for verified accounts and can be changed in **Settings → Profile**. When credit applies, the verified email is visible in Git history. [GitHub credit and profile settings](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model#gateway-profile-and-github-credit)

For channel requests routed through shared main chat, delegated work credits the verified requester when they have enabled Git credit. Publishing directly from main does not add automatic human credit. A different person’s request to steer waits for its own turn rather than using the permissions of work already underway.



##### Git co-author credit sources


- GitHub Enterprise co-author credit. [GitHub credit and profile settings](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model#gateway-profile-and-github-credit) · [#173513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173513) · [23a5696](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/23a569674bca84b34e3e591a75a7cd6150e72d31) · [Issue #173512](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173512)
- Credit for delegated channel requests. [Git co-author credit](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model) · [#176513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176513) · [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus)

Thanks [@galiniliev](https://github.com/galiniliev) and [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus).



#### Optional GitHub PR attribution

You can add a “Made with OpenClaw” footer to new GitHub pull requests. The setting starts off. Turn on **Add OpenClaw attribution to pull requests** under **Settings → Profile → Identity**, and skip the footer for individual PRs when you like. OpenClaw applies the footer when creating PRs for you, and agent-created PRs through the GitHub CLI or shell use it on a best-effort basis. Incognito conversations skip automatic attribution. See the [attribution guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model#optional-openclaw-pull-request-attribution).



##### Sources and complete change list

#### GitHub lookups in chat

With the [GitHub tools](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/github), permitted agents can find issues or pull requests in a named public repository, read public issue, pull request or commit links, and inspect the end of a completed public Actions job log. Sandboxed agents can use the tools through the Gateway without GitHub credentials or outbound GitHub access inside the sandbox. Results can be incomplete or truncated.

With [GitHub Enterprise previews](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/github#session-bound-enterprise-previews) configured, you can open issue, pull request and commit links from the current session’s authorized repository in the Control UI, including private repositories. A configured [GitHub App](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/github-identity) can provide short-lived, repository-scoped credentials for authorized foreground reads, with access checked for the signed-in operator.

With [GitHub inspection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.5/docs/gateway/config-tools/github-identity.md) enabled, paste a link to a pull request you opened and ask your agent to check its status and which branches and commits it compares. This includes pull requests created outside OpenClaw, from a session you can access. Inspection is read-only on the configured GitHub host and uses your verified linked author account’s access to private repositories. Links from Files changed, Commits and Checks work too.



##### GitHub lookup sources


- [Read public links](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172692) and [search public issues and pull requests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172779). See the [GitHub plugin guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/plugins/github.md) for access and search details. Thanks [@shakkernerd](https://github.com/shakkernerd).
- [Read completed public Actions job logs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176147) · [commit 19d311e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/19d311e002468b6bdd3a76c507ce93a8c6b4bfd2). Long logs return up to 64 KiB from the end and mark earlier output as omitted. The selected identity needs Actions read access and the log must be available. Thanks [@shakkernerd](https://github.com/shakkernerd).
- [Session-bound Enterprise previews](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173712) and [GitHub App credentials for authorized foreground reads](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173668). Thanks [@galiniliev](https://github.com/galiniliev).
- [Inspect pull requests you opened](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178055) · [commit 01c2c602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01c2c602d461058d07d2828d3ac52006ff302d9d). Thanks [@shakkernerd](https://github.com/shakkernerd).

  [Shared destination previews #181904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181904) · [commit 87c7b33](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/87c7b33a1b40f83372d5de0df711fb621c916778) · [Shared session-store reads #183322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183322) · [commit db4d0d5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/db4d0d5dbb2686889da2f994801e543980b0e07c) · [Manual runs and SQLite heartbeat state #183324](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183324) · [commit c554849](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c554849c28df0733bd2d0e13bae874912fba4d44) · [Avoid full scans for missing delivery routes #183977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183977) · [Shared fallback sessions #186155](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186155) · [commit f70acef](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f70acef7e48d2b9ea2520f0def67360192d0075f) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Removes the extra wait for the next status check from scheduled runs waiting on generated images, music or video. The run can move on when the media is ready or queued for delivery.
  [Scheduled media waits #182925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182925) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces repeated permission checks as scheduled agent runs continue. OpenClaw can record usage and activity for completed work after operator access is revoked, while new privileged tool actions still require current access.
  [Scheduled turn checks #182066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182066) · [commit 85d123d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/85d123d13e594c1310b28038c91516d58aad6ebf) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Replaces long inspection URLs in Telegram and Discord cron completion messages and failure alerts with a short **Inspect run** link. These links appear when the Control UI is enabled and `gateway.publicOrigin` is configured.
  [Cron delivery guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md) · [Issue #150029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150029) · [Inspect run links #183958](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183958) · [commit 31c6d54](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/31c6d5440b24b91929e9d472d17f652901e7c133) · Thanks [@obviyus](https://github.com/obviyus) for co-authoring and [@rwesmarter](https://github.com/rwesmarter) for the report.
- Reduces the data loaded to browse [cron run history](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs) or find a run’s transcript, and uses fewer SQLite queries for long histories while preserving totals, filters and completion order.
  [History pages and transcript links #174175](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174175) · [commit afe03ab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/afe03ab7249237d27a09f53605cca3907e442ab9) · [SQLite history queries #174889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174889) · [commit f211df0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f211df0fd059135c1e2b349f17e665ef04af60e9) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Changes self-scoped automation lists to best effort while the job list is changing. If an automation cannot find itself, repeat the lookup.
  [Self-scoped lookup #174349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174349) · [commit 7a2f433](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7a2f433410ed0923c39f36028c2f43df8096e58b) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Removes a redundant database lookup when the Gateway prepares prompts for scheduled automations.
  [Prompt preparation #180816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180816) · [commit 691a3e1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/691a3e1f13172a19db94c2beba4d5e2962fb6175) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) and [@fuller-stack-dev](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev).
- Cuts an extra database read when the cron queue checks running jobs and cancellations for specific requests.
  [Cron queue checks #183477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183477) · [commit 18e6653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/18e665348fa58cbb5658a06b1fc66c99c36429c0) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces database work when cleaning up completed isolated cron runs without removing the job’s conversation history. Cleanup also skips a full usage recalculation when the transcript, access and agent attribution remain unchanged.
  [Isolated run cleanup #174413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174413) · [Usage recalculation #175154](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175154) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces the work needed to save sessions for isolated scheduled runs while preserving edits such as renaming or pinning a session during a run.
  [Scheduled session saves #175249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175249) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces background work for scheduled jobs when checking and updating schedules, recording results, recovering runs and maintaining history. Event- and stream-triggered automations also need less maintenance work.
  [Run history maintenance #183937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183937) · [commit c81dd51](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c81dd517eeb49536348b1ac128f4b64d22aafd86) · [Event and stream maintenance #183949](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183949) · [commit dcd0f38](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dcd0f38acf7874c927b9e0f60797444b2f4efc0a) · [Recording and startup recovery #184598](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184598) · [commit 16e4b17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/16e4b179efa7793934effe71d17dbb97d0531453) · [Rebuilding job lists #184602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184602) · [commit 82cdd47](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/82cdd47fed6229e166d85553c598c61170c77f99) · [Queued schedule updates #185724](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185724) · [commit e28d765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e28d76535a4007dcf0fa1f4c48fb87f832e55840) · [Workspace checks and timeout destinations #185801](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185801) · [commit abf88cb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/abf88cbc0a4484faeab8f80db4ce35200f6ff53e) · [Skip unchanged schedule refreshes and streamline cleanup #186245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186245) · [commit 8fc14c9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8fc14c9d0ebff878d7c496bac1223d5eaa928d71) · [Skip unchanged-job checks and unneeded post-run maintenance #187057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187057) · Thanks [@vincentkoc](https://github.com/vincentkoc) for #184598 and [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) for the other changes.
- Reduces temporary memory use when reusing a prepared cron job store and reduces Gateway CPU and memory work when reloading scheduled jobs, especially when their definitions have not changed.
  [Prepared store #185176](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185176) · [Job reloads #186397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186397) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

##### Files and panels beside chat

###### Files and outputs

- Adds **Download** to the Files list and preview toolbar in the [Control UI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui), including for files too large to preview. Individual downloads use the saved file on supported session workspaces and require the Control UI and Gateway to share an origin.
  [#172042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172042) · Thanks to [@jacobtomlinson](https://github.com/jacobtomlinson). Downloads are unavailable on node workspaces whose bridges only support whole-file reads.
- Adds **Attach to session** to an open file’s menu in [Control UI chat](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui). The attachment includes unsaved text edits without saving the file, and goes out when you send the message.
  Attach eligible files, images and PDFs from the viewer. The composer applies its usual upload permissions and size limits. [#179609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179609) · [f6580eb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f6580eb85f4db861cbb8b585abd95035ed6de73b) · Thanks [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).
- Keeps loaded files browsable and searchable on desktop and in the legacy Files view through a refresh failure or retry, with folders still open. Desktop and mobile Outputs retain their rows and keyboard focus. A newer preview of the same file can appear while an older request is still pending.
  <a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180031">#180031</a> · <a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/24b180b712fa0c5861dc7a8c5b3c94bc00f0d6ca">commit 24b180b7</a>. Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Collapses the Files tree when you open a reader from the file list and remembers your choice as you switch between open tabs.
  <span><a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181903">#181903</a>, <a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d25ac789c15a36aa89614abc5bc84e8504ecb4a8">d25ac789</a>. Thanks to <a href="https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski">@vyctorbrzezowski</a>.</span>
- Makes searching and filtering the desktop Files panel more responsive in large folders that contain only files. Browser Find and screen-reader browsing cover only rendered filenames in these folders. Use Files search to look across the whole workspace.
  [#184230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184230) · [3daa072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3daa0726b521041ac8d8b8234249cf34a0ee72fe). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces the wait to open folders or search Files in large managed guest workspaces, while still showing up-to-date files.
  [#186616](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186616). Thanks to shakkernerd.
- Reduces unnecessary browser CPU work when you expand folders in large Control UI workspaces.
  [#185338](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185338) · [1faa6f1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1faa6f1f9c71022843e7f314c7a15f91ac5e26cd). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Avoids a redundant disk check when you open the top level of a local session’s Files view.
  [#185550](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185550) · [a9e4426](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a9e4426d924c5d18522d8af84741ce8b43f180e1) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces the work needed to open or refresh files and diffs in a conversation’s current workspace.
  [#184621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184621) ([`f94b6a6f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f94b6a6f6b7fe52bfc21648021d8f1d8b89be8db)). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces the processing needed to list session and conversation artifacts.
  Session artifacts — Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete). [#182205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182205) · [`d2425ddc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d2425ddc44cde81084e824ac2d0f8209162a928d); Conversation artifacts — [#186159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186159) · [Commit fcb68764](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fcb687646ac7595b214f27abdf6bf4af783d9016) · Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

###### Changes and pull requests

- Adds automatic retries when session checkout changes take a while to load, keeping the loading view or the previous diff in place while **Review** is visible. API clients can opt in with `poll: true` on `sessions.diff`. Retry a `computing: true` response to get the diff when it’s ready.
  <span>[#179091](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179091) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete) · [Chat guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat)</span>
- Cuts extra Git work when opening uncommitted session diffs that need no starting comparison and uncached diffs in checkouts without a branch.
  - Reduces Git work when opening uncommitted session diffs that do not need comparison with the starting changes, and when Review hides edits that predate the session. It also cuts extra Git work when looking up a fallback comparison branch.
    Session diffs — Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete). [#176842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176842) · [commit 5ec30bf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5ec30bfc7216adeb622700464db6dccae368e17e); Uncommitted changes in Review — <span><a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181918">#181918</a>, <a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7480093408d4c0d0c29bb1070cfe1ea40a64f6d7">74800934</a>. Thanks to <a href="https://github.com/steipete">@steipete</a>.</span>

  - Cuts unnecessary Git work when opening an uncached session diff in a checkout that isn’t on a branch, without changing what the diff shows.
    <a href="https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185967">#185967</a> · Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete)
- Reduces work when refreshing session diffs and sharing them with multiple viewers, and can make an eligible file’s patch visible again after an extra hard link is removed.
  - Reduces work and memory use when refreshing session diffs, including checkouts with many untracked files. Eligible non-Windows checkouts can reuse an unchanged result while still checking for real edits. Removing an extra hard link can also make an eligible file’s patch visible again.
    Session diff previews — Repeat-read reuse applies to eligible non-Windows checkouts. [#177195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177195). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete); Cache reuse and miss reasons — [Prometheus metrics](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/prometheus) [#177762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177762) · [55e36fef](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/55e36fef7252073b5beed033272cfd2880958d34). Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete); Untracked-file memory use — [#184284](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184284) · [8357196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/835719681b2141b35910b15bb7128b7bb2c33180). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete); Unchanged diff polls — [#185684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185684) · [1e85438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1e85438770195284b5102c3402c111602f2dd2dc) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete); Checking for outside edits — [#186222](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186222) · [Commit 63ba4974](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/63ba4974f67c1eba483f8b7121c2bf7416d75ae4) · Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  - Reduces the work of serving a session diff to several viewers, refreshing diff summaries in very large local checkouts, and waiting for the Changes summary while other Git reads are busy. Reopening full diffs in large non-sparse checkouts and refreshing oversized diffs without patch previews also takes less work.
    [Shared diff reads #177329](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177329) · [Commit 5387b20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5387b207cdabf09c71c952d560ca98c89e9cdc20) · [Changes summary #177386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177386) · [Commit 589f812](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/589f81214a04b8a8075c9de6c770e621ad7d1a07) · [Large checkout summaries #177476](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177476) · [Commit fea0de1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fea0de1046b4554478d599f99d801859181a301c) · [Control UI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui) · [Oversized diffs #185831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185831) · [Commit 3f8844b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f8844b4b403f44dd4fdeae93306d6407613d136) · [Full diff reopening #186170](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186170) · [Commit bf72e96b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf72e96b39a2d6299d7d2d99c7a9d6a3bdb7a512). Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Reduces repeated Git work in the Changes panel for clean checkouts and for checkouts with nested repositories or submodules.
  - Cuts repeat scans for clean Git checkouts in the Changes panel, including when opening **All changes**. Committed branch changes remain visible and later edits are picked up.
    Control UI Changes panel — [#185087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185087) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete); Changes panel — [#186210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186210) · [Commit 989a897d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/989a897df2d5f078e0fa54aac8c13907c33c6fa0) · Thanks to [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).

  - Reduces repeated Git work in the [Changes panel](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui) by reusing unchanged diffs for checkouts with nested repositories, submodules or an external ignore file, and by cutting checks when a large checkout can only show a summary. Changes to the ignore file or a submodule commit still refresh the diff. Automatic checks of folders that are not Git checkouts wait briefly before trying again, while manual refresh checks immediately.
    [Diff reuse #178400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178400) · [Changes polling #178574](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178574) · [Polling changes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e5302ee39c532afe0e2874990867b06f1e523bf5) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Lets the shared Git read finish in the background after you cancel your view and stop waiting for the result.
  [#173523](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173523) · [a05b8f6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a05b8f6e552c11340df8ab706e7a8ab180701dec) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Shows additions and deletions in desktop chat Details → Environment, with a control to open the uncommitted diff.
  [Desktop Environment line counts #171794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171794) · [11.5 Details implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-environment.tsx) · Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete).
- Adds a mobile pull request publication review for sessions with an eligible branch or retained publication. It shows available repository, branch, account and publication status before you act. Opening the review does not publish the pull request.
  [Mobile publication review #176416](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176416) · Thanks [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).
- Puts pull request status and a checks badge beside the title in compact session Details. The actions menu brings together repository and change information, checks, CI monitoring, and options to open, copy or hide the pull request. Hidden checks and monitoring views stop refreshing. If details fail to load, you can retry, and an out-of-date page offers a reload when it will not interrupt your work.
  [Pull request Details #176424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176424) · Thanks [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

###### Chat Details and activity

- Adds sections for outputs, saved progress, subagents and processes in Chat Details, including process previews you can open to see output or stop eligible processes.
  - Adds sections in [Details](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat) in the [Control UI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui) for session outputs, saved task progress, subagents and running processes, alongside available [environment and context views](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/panels).
